details.description: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct is an instruction-tuned chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, part of the Qwen3-Next series that introduces a hybrid attention architecture combining Gated DeltaNet linear attention with Gated Attention, alongside a high-sparsity Mixture-of-Experts design with 80 billion total parameters and about 3 billion activated per token. Qwen's model card states it supports only non-thinking (instruct) mode, without generating extended reasoning traces, and documents integration with the Qwen-Agent framework for tool use and agentic tasks. It is text-only, with no vision input, and is released under the Apache 2.0 license.
advantages: Scores 80.6 on MMLU-Pro, a knowledge benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 69.5% on AIME25, a competition math benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 56.6% on LiveCodeBench v6, a coding benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.
Only about 3 billion of its 80 billion parameters are activated per token via its Mixture-of-Experts design, per its Hugging Face model card.
Documented as integrating with the Qwen-Agent framework for tool calling and agentic workflows, per its Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: Supports only non-thinking (instruct) mode and does not generate extended reasoning/thinking traces; Qwen offers a separate Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking model for that, per its Hugging Face model card.
Text-only: no image or vision input, per its Hugging Face model card.
use_cases: General-purpose conversational assistant and instruction following
Agentic tool use via the Qwen-Agent framework

notes: Large context-length conflict: the catalog lists max_input_tokens and max_output_tokens as 4,096, but the Hugging Face model card, Qwen's own Qwen3-Next launch blog, and Fireworks' hosted page for this exact model all state a native context length of 262,144 tokens (validated up to about 1,010,000 tokens via YaRN scaling) -- a two-orders-of-magnitude gap from the catalog facts. Per instructions the catalog figure was kept and no specific context/output-token number is stated in the description; flagging this for review since it is a much larger discrepancy than typical rounding. Fireworks' hosted listing separately states function calling is not supported on that platform, which appears to contradict the maker's own tool-use/Qwen-Agent documentation, so that claim was left out rather than used as a disadvantage. A Qwen maker blog post for Qwen3-Next was found, linked directly from the Hugging Face model card (qwen.ai/blog?id=4074cca8...); it has been added to sources and confirms the architecture and context-length figures above. No dedicated Qwen3-Next GitHub repository was found -- the QwenLM GitHub org's Qwen3-Next repo path now redirects to a newer 'Qwen3.8' repo -- so github_url remains null. No source found declaring this model deprecated or superseded.
